text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A special Sunday Times report finds that the insurance industry in Nigeria is a "big rip-off, distrusted and riddled with fraud."
- Twelve students members of the Black Axe cult society have been arrested in eastern Nigeria.
- Absence of regulation on import of electronic products has turned Nigeria into a dumping ground for all kinds of gadgets.
- Provisional ruling council may meet this week to finally take a decision on the proposal by political parties to postpone state governorship elections to next year.
- Nigerian Breweries exports rise to 19.2 million naira in 1996 from 10.3 million naira in 1995, says managing director Felix Ohiwerei.
- Niger Delta Environmental survey sponsored by the local unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group completes first part of its assignment, according to its executive secretary Jonathan Amakiri.
- Demand for foreign exchange at the weekly auction has declined by 60 percent over the last six weeks.
- Nigeria's joint venture multinational oil companies are considering shutting down oil operations for 30 days to protest the 40 percent cut in their budgets by the military government.
